name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-delay-f1f6

dma_host_support.reason: the host adds the declared dma_response_delay to mwb_stall/mwb_ack for each accepted master beat and measures the wait of every response; the case line reports dma_wait_min/max, dma_stall_ticks, dma_max_consecutive_stalls and dma_delay_evidence, and the pass criterion refuses a declared delay that was not observed
where: scripts/inprocess_obi_apb_f1f4_spike.cpp (Master.delay = DMA_RESPONSE_DELAY + the write-data-late cycle; per-accept accept_tick; dma_delay_evidence)

notes: same timer/target, DMA profile/behavior and four-word block as configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-f1f6.json; this copy adds the delay/backpressure declaration and what a run has to observe

dma_response_delay 2 declares two host-generated stall ticks before each DMA master response; evidence: runs/round1-dma-a/delay (dma_wait_min 3 = 2 declared ticks plus the host's one pending tick, dma_delayed_acks 8/8, dma_max_consecutive_stalls 4)

observation expectations: every accepted master read/write response is held 2 ticks, the four-word data payload is unchanged by the stall, the level-sensitive completion IRQ still arrives, and the declared clear write still deasserts it.  A run that cannot measure per-response wait ticks reports dma_delay_evidence unknown and fails the correspondence check rather than passing silently
the ZipDMA profile's nominal 1 Hz is a simulation scheduling value, not hardware timing; assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives CPU, timer and DMA
